title: Performative Debias with Fair-exposure Optimization Driven by Strategic Agents in Recommender Systems

problem.claim: Popularity bias in recommender systems can impair two-sided-market dynamics and overshadow potentially interesting long-tail items.

gap.claim: Despite substantial research, addressing this issue remains challenging.

contributions.claim: A dynamic re-ranking approach with fair-exposure optimization driven by strategic agents.
An end-to-end optimization process using differentiable ranking operators to jointly target recommendation accuracy and fairness.
A performativity-based mechanism modeling how strategic learning can influence content creators to shift toward fairness and incentivize tail-item features.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report comprehensive experiments on public and industrial datasets.
The authors report that the proposed method is effective and dominant, especially for revealing the potential of tail items.

narrative_sequence.summary: Popularity bias harms recommender-system market dynamics and reduces visibility of long-tail items.
The issue remains difficult despite extensive research.
The paper develops dynamic fair-exposure re-ranking driven by strategic producer agents.
Differentiable ranking operators optimize accuracy and fairness jointly, while performativity models strategic shifts toward fairer item features.
Experiments on public and industrial datasets are reported to support effectiveness, particularly for tail items.

source_observation.claim: The approach jointly optimizes recommendation accuracy and fair exposure while modeling strategic changes by content creators.

interpretation.claim: Debiasing may be more effective when recommendation decisions and adaptive producer behavior are optimized as an interacting system.

application.claim: Use dynamic ranking objectives that account for both exposure fairness and strategic changes to item features.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when strategic adaptation improves fairness or how the method behaves outside the reported datasets.

unknowns: Specific dataset names, experimental settings, baselines, metrics, and numerical results are not provided.
The abstract does not define the fair-exposure objective or differentiable ranking operators.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported effectiveness or dominance.
